items.prose: Pre-war 35mm civil defense training reels underwent autocatalytic nitrate breakdown. The film base liquefied into an acidic, amber-colored sticky syrup giving off pungent nitrogen dioxide fumes that dissolved the aluminum storage cans.

Exothermic decomposition inside a sealed, unventilated archive locker caused the internal temperature of twelve nitrate film reels to rise above 40°C. The film auto-ignited without an external spark, blowing out the vault door with a searing flash fire that required zero oxygen to burn.

Sulfur gases from nearby battery charging rooms attacked the silver gelatin emulsion on historical 16mm construction reels. The image layer oxidized into a reflective, metallic bronze mirror that completely obscured the filmed engineering blueprints.

Loss of camphor plasticizer caused long, needle-like white crystals to grow across the film edges inside the steel canisters. Deprived of plasticizer, the film warped into a tight corkscrew spiral that jammed the projector sprocket teeth.

Hundreds of microfiche sheets containing pre-war medical records underwent severe de-acetylation. Opening the steel cabinet released a choking cloud of pure acetic acid vapor (85 ppm) that burned the archivist's eyes and corroded the steel reader lenses.

A momentary pause in the projector mechanism exposed a single frame of aged nitrate film to the carbon-arc lamp beam. The film ignited instantly, sending flames racing through the upper feed magazine and incinerating the projection booth in under twenty seconds.

Five hundred feet of nine-inch wide aerial reconnaissance roll film decomposed and melted together under its own weight. The roll consolidated into a solid, glass-hard brown cylinder resembling natural amber, permanently entombing the pre-war photographic intelligence.
